affected_boundaries: post-merge worker progress to campaign action readiness

observed_behavior: An open-plan worker's next undelivered tasklet commit leaves its assignment MERGED and blocks campaign actions with a cleanup ancestry diagnostic.
expected_behavior: The original assignment resumes ACTIVE work without blocking independent actions, while new integration still requires authenticated delivery.
causal_mechanism: Reconciliation replaces the integrated milestone revision with current worker HEAD but does not leave MERGED before the next delivery, so cleanup validation consumes a revision from a different execution phase.

anti_pattern.structural_description: A lifecycle projection updates its evidence identity without transitioning the state whose invariant governs that evidence.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: Ordinary in-progress evidence is judged by an integrated-cleanup invariant and becomes a campaign-wide failure.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: An integrated milestone followed by new unfinished work in an active plan returns to active execution before cleanup invariants are evaluated.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: The effective assignment state returns surviving active-plan workers to ACTIVE when dirty or unintegrated, retaining the authenticated delivery and closed-plan cleanup gates.

applicability_conditions: Surviving worker resumes dirty or unintegrated work before its next authenticated delivery
known_non_matches: New authenticated delivery awaiting rebase or integration
confirmation_evidence: Real-Git differential changed only worker revision: integrated passed, undelivered descendant blocked ready-actions.
Extended second-delivery regression failed before repair, then passed dirty work, committed work, and closed-plan negative control; all 42 scheduler tests passed.
regression_proofs: tests/campaign-orchestration.test.js: an open merged plan accepts a second delivery from its original assignment
